summary:
SPECIAL-VALUE SWEEP OF THE NUMERIC LEVERS OF EVAL AND DATA. 26 numeric levers found by enumerating each package's levers.py for a Lever whose default is int or float and not bool -- EVAL 15 (12 int, 3 float), DATA 11 (8 int, 3 float). 26 x 4 values (nan, inf, -inf, 0) = 104 primary cells, each driven in a FRESH SUBPROCESS as the generated env var PREFIX_FIELD through a real spine.assemble.build() and then as far down as the package runs today: for DATA that is open_areas -> data_plan -> draw_stream (all three land BEFORE compose()'s halt at row 29, CAP.startup_refusals) and for EVAL that is curve_period, the package's only non-stub entry point. Every cell also ran the real spine.compose.compose(environ=...). A 44-cell confirmation pass re-ran all DATA cells under DATA_SOURCE=real (the shipped default is synthetic, on which corpus_cap / val_cap / holdout_frac are structurally inert) plus 2 baselines and targeted probes: 150 process runs total.

OUTCOME COUNTS OVER THE 104 PRIMARY CELLS: REFUSED_BY_NAME 25, REFUSED_BADLY 45, ACCEPTED_HARMFUL 4, ACCEPTED_INERT 1, ACCEPTED_LEGITIMATE 6, UNREACHABLE_TODAY 23, CRASHED 0.

THE HEADLINE IS NOT IN EITHER PACKAGE, IT IS IN THE SPINE. src/spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce catches only (TypeError, ValueError). int(float('inf')) raises OverflowError, which is in neither -- so EVERY int lever in the tree at inf or -inf refuses with a bare `OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer`, naming no lever, no value, and not even the sign. That is 40 of my 104 cells and 110 int levers tree-wide (measured: 262 levers, 110 int, 97 float, 55 other). The nan half is already sound for ints -- int(float('nan')) raises ValueError, so coerce turns it into `EVAL_WINDOWS='nan' is not a int`, a refusal that names itself.

THE FAB_BALANCE SHAPE IS PRESENT IN DATA, ONCE, AND IT IS THE SAME MECHANISM: the two exposure guards. DATA_EXPOSURE_MAX=nan assembles, data_plan builds a Plan, and spine/gate.py::Gate prints `Gate data.exposure_max: armed, did not fire (0.75 vs nan)` -- reachable=True on a comparison `max(vals) > nan` that is False for every possible value. These are exactly the two guards goal B's add-an-area experiment rests on. No NaN reaches a tensor anywhere in my surface; nothing on this surface is critical.

EVAL IS ALMOST ENTIRELY LATENT. 8 of its 9 entry points (curve_probe, holdout_probe, null_excess, generate, coherence, verdicts, wrongness_probe, verification_fit) raise NotImplementedError naming P5/P6 -- proven by calling all eight. Only curve_period runs. So 14 of EVAL's 15 numeric levers have no live consumer, and every value that survives coercion (nan/inf/-inf on the 3 floats, 0 on 11 ints) freezes into the Config with ZERO warnings and stops there. That is 23 UNREACHABLE_TODAY cells, not 23 inert ones: EVAL_GEN_TEMP=nan is a NaN sitting in the frozen Config of goal A's headline sampler, waiting for P6 to divide by it.

WHAT THE RULING PHASE NEEDS FROM THE DENOMINATOR: on this surface a central rule in src/spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce that refused non-finite floats by name would wrongly refuse NOTHING -- no lever in EVAL or DATA declares nan, inf or -inf as a sentinel, and no cell here needed one. A central rule that refused 0 would be wrong six times; those six are listed in legitimate_specials, and two of them (DATA_PHASE_LIVE=0, DATA_PHASES=0) are declared in the lever's own text or comment.

findings.lever: ALL 20 int levers on this surface (EVAL: coh_len coh_seeds curve_every gen_domains gen_len gen_samples genuine_min holdout_windows null_draws verify_fit_steps windows wrong_inject; DATA: corpus_cap n_processes phase_live phases seg_max seg_min stream_bytes val_cap)
findings.detail: src/spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce does `elif isinstance(d, int): v = int(float(raw))` inside `try: ... except (TypeError, ValueError)`. int(float('inf')) raises OverflowError, which that tuple does not name, so the LeverError that would have said `PREFIX_FIELD='inf' is not a int` never runs and a bare `OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer` escapes build(). The operator is told neither which env var they typed, nor what they typed, nor the SIGN -- +inf and -inf produce byte-identical messages. The nan path in the same function is correct (int(float('nan')) raises ValueError and is caught), which is what makes this a one-token omission rather than a design choice. BREADTH: 40 of my 104 cells; measured tree-wide there are 262 levers, of which 110 are int, so this covers 110 levers under one edit. It is a refusal and not a corruption -- nothing runs afterwards -- so the damage is diagnostic, but the tree's own idiom is a refusal that names itself, and this is the single widest place it does not.

EVAL_WINDOWS=inf python3 -c "import sys,os;sys.path.insert(0,'src')\nfrom spine.assemble import build\ntry: build(environ=os.environ)\nexcept Exception as e: print(type(e).__name__+': '+str(e))"
  EVAL_WINDOWS=inf  -> OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer
  EVAL_WINDOWS=-inf -> OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer
  DATA_SEG_MIN=inf  -> OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer
  DATA_VAL_CAP=-inf -> OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer
  EVAL_WINDOWS=nan  -> LeverError: EVAL_WINDOWS='nan' is not a int      <-- the good case, same function

findings.value: -inf (1 cell; the same cell as the finding above, called out separately)
findings.detail: src/eval/api.py::curve_period carries a hand-written, switch-guarded, correctly-named refusal for a negative learning-curve period (REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD, shipped True, added under the owner's 2026-09-04 ruling). At -5 it speaks and is exemplary. At -inf the spine's coercion raises OverflowError first, so the package's own good refusal never gets to run and the operator sees a message from a file they have never heard of. This is the concrete cost of the coercion hole above: it does not merely fail to name a lever, it SILENCES a package that was ready to. Fixing coerce fixes this too -- I list it because it is the cleanest single demonstration that the fix belongs in the spine and not in 110 read sites.

findings.detail: This is the FAB_BALANCE=nan shape, in DATA, on the two guards that stand closest to goal B. Both are floats, so src/spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce admits nan without comment; src/data/api.py::data_plan then evaluates `max(vals) > float(dat.exposure_max)` and `skew > float(dat.exposure_skew)`, both of which are False for EVERY possible value when the threshold is nan, and hands the answer to spine/gate.py::Gate with the default reachable=True. The printed line is `Gate data.exposure_max: armed, did not fire (0.75 vs nan)` -- the exact three-state collapse src/spine/gate.py exists to refuse, stated in its own docstring: 'fired=False, reachable=True means the mechanism ran and its condition was not met -- a measurement. reachable=False means the condition CANNOT be met on this configuration, which is not a measurement at all.' WHAT IS LOST: these two guards are the only startup statement of whether a held-out score measures generalisation or repetition (src/data/levers.py::DATALevers, exposure_max/exposure_skew comments, ISSUES P3-H22: an added area seen 2.1x while the original was 28% sampled makes 'adding py cost eng X b/B' indistinguishable from 'py was memorised and eng was skimmed'). At nan the run is unguarded against exactly that confound and the report says the guard was armed. Not critical: no NaN reaches a tensor, nothing downstream consumes the gate today, and the numbers ARE printed beside the verdict so a careful reader sees the nan. The defect is the word, and the word is what the report is read for.

findings.detail: Same mechanism as the nan cells, one notch weaker. At threshold=inf no finite exposure can ever exceed it, so the gate is unreachable in fact and prints `armed, did not fire (0.75 vs inf)`. It differs from nan in that 'inf means no cap' is a reading a person might intend -- but it is NOT declared anywhere: src/data/levers.py::DATALevers says only 'above which the data plan is flagged', and the code has no inf branch. So an operator who disables the guard on purpose gets a report that says it was armed, and an operator who disables it by accident gets no signal at all. Low because it takes a deliberate typed 'inf' to reach and the arithmetic is printed beside the verdict. Note the other two arms are honest: at -inf and at 0 the gate genuinely FIRES, because 0.75 > 0.0 and 0.75 > -inf are true; those are in legitimate_specials.

findings.detail: holdout_frac is a float, so the spine admits all three without comment; the first read is inside src/data/api.py::open_areas, `frac_bytes[label] = int(len(blob) * float(dat.holdout_frac))`, which raises a bare `ValueError: cannot convert float NaN to integer` (nan) or `OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer` (both infinities). No lever named, no value quoted, and the traceback points at a line in a package the operator did not touch. THIS IS THE ONE CASE ON MY SURFACE WHERE THE PACKAGE ITSELF HAS THE ANSWER AND DOES NOT GIVE IT: forty lines further down, the SAME function refuses holdout_frac=0 beautifully -- `area 'eng' computed a 0-byte held-out block: min(int(2000000 * 0.0), 4000000) == 0 from DATA_HOLDOUT_FRAC=0.0 and DATA_VAL_CAP=4000000 ... raise DATA_HOLDOUT_FRAC or DATA_VAL_CAP`. The refusal that names itself already exists in this function; it just sits after the int() that blows up first. Medium: it is a startup refusal, nothing is corrupted, but goal B's entire held-out measurement hangs off this lever and the failure mode is a stack trace instead of a sentence.

findings.detail: DATA does its part honestly and then the run dies two packages away. open_areas, data_plan and draw_stream all succeed; draw_stream returns a ZERO-BYTE Stream and prints an exemplary gate that names the lever and the value -- `Gate data.stream_draw: armed, did not fire (0 vs 0) -- DATA_STREAM_BYTES=0: no phase had a byte to fill, so the draw loop never ran a body and this call drew nothing in 0 rng draw(s)`. But nothing REFUSES, so the composition root walks on to TOK.tokenize, which calls spine/derive.py::bytes_per_token on an empty segmentation and raises `ValueError: bytes_per_token: n_tokens=0 -- cannot measure compression over zero tokens. The caller has an empty segmentation, which is the defect.` That message names TOK's caller as the defect when the actual cause is a DATA lever the operator typed. Reproduced through the real spine.compose.compose(), not a hand-assembled prefix. Side effect worth recording: at stream_bytes=0 the synthetic areas shrink from 60000 to 10000 bytes each and `Gate data.exposure_skew` reports value=inf and FIRES, because src/data/api.py::data_plan computes `skew = max(vals)/min(vals) if min(vals) > 0 else float('inf')` on an all-zero exposure vector. Medium: a startup failure, but it is the one cell on my surface where the operator's typed lever and the raised message are in different packages.

findings.detail: 0 has a MEANING here and the lever declaration states it: src/data/levers.py::DATALevers, corpus_cap comment -- 'New default should be 0 = read what is on disk ... 0 must FIRST mean no cap at the read site (today it would mean read nothing)'. Today it means read nothing, and reading nothing produces `CorpusError: area 'eng' at 'data/train/eng' holds no usable bytes. Refused rather than dropped: ...` -- a CorpusError, so it is the package's own named exception type, but it names the AREA and the PATH and not the lever the operator set. An operator who set DATA_CORPUS_CAP=0 following the census recommendation in that very comment is told their corpus is empty. On the shipped default (DATA_SOURCE=synthetic) the same value is completely inert and honestly so: `Gate data.corpus_cap_trip: UNREACHABLE (None vs 2000000) -- DATA_SOURCE=synthetic: each area is generated to the size the sampler needs and nothing is read off disk`. Low: the refusal is loud, at startup, from the right package, and only the noun is wrong.

findings.detail: UNREACHABLE BECAUSE THE CONSUMER IS A P4-ERA STUB, NOT BECAUSE ANYTHING REFUSED. All three coerce cleanly, freeze into the EVAL Config with build() returning an EMPTY warnings list, and `cfg.given()` records them -- then stop, because src/eval/api.py::verdicts, ::generate and ::coherence all raise NotImplementedError naming P5/P6. Verified by calling all eight EVAL consumers; every one is a stub. WHAT ARMS THE MOMENT P6 LANDS, read off the levers' own declarations: EVAL_GEN_TEMP is 'Sampling temperature for every generated continuation, printed AND SCORED alike', read by both GENERATION and COHERENCE from this one Config -- gen_temp=nan puts a NaN into the divisor of goal A's headline sampler and gen_temp=0 puts a zero there; EVAL_AFF_MIN is 'Minimum share of a domain's expert-usage mass at which an expert counts as SERVING it', so at nan every `share > aff_min` is False and the affiliation table reports that no expert serves any domain; EVAL_GENUINE_SIL is the silhouette floor whose predecessor test 'never bound and silently reduced to a size threshold' (the untrippable-guard class, 60 of the survey's 475 records) -- at nan it reverts to exactly that. None of these three levers declares nan, inf or -inf as a sentinel. Medium and not low: the hole is real, it is in the package whose whole job is measurement, and it is invisible today only because nobody has written the code that would trip on it.

findings.detail: All eleven resolve to 0, freeze, and reach nothing: their consumers are the eight P5/P6 stubs. None of the eleven declares 0 as a sentinel. Two of them have the failure WRITTEN DOWN ALREADY, which is what makes this medium rather than low. (1) EVAL_NULL_DRAWS: src/eval/levers.py::EVALLevers says in its own comment 'ISSUES P1-L44 (this knob at 0 -> ZeroDivisionError) and L45 (at 1 -> the 2-sigma test is a rubber stamp, since a one-sample null has zero spread) both want a floor of 2 ... the floor belongs in the nulls module that consumes this, as a refusal at construction'. That module is src/eval/api.py::null_excess, a stub -- so the declared home of the refusal does not exist yet, and every 2-sigma verdict in the tree is judged against this null. (2) EVAL_WRONG_INJECT: its comment records that the unguarded version 'raised IndexError and took the WHOLE eval battery down AFTER training and checkpointing had completed -- a full run's compute spent and no report'. The remaining nine (windows=0, holdout_windows=0, coh_seeds=0, coh_len=0, gen_samples=0, gen_domains=0, gen_len=0, genuine_min=0, verify_fit_steps=0) are all sample sizes or thresholds where 0 means 'measure nothing' and would produce an empty Sample rather than a refusal. This is the latent, not the absent, class: it arms on the day P5/P6 land.

legitimate_specials:
DATA_PHASE_LIVE=0 -- SENTINEL, DECLARED IN THE HELP TEXT ITSELF: 'How many areas are live in each phase of the GENERATED schedule; 0 derives it from the area count' (src/data/levers.py::DATALevers, phase_live). The read site is src/data/api.py::data_plan, `int(dat.phase_live) or None`, and the comment there says '0 IS A SENTINEL, NOT A VALUE, and it is the literal that keeps the derivation where it belongs'. Verified: plan and stream are byte-identical to baseline. A central rule refusing 0 WOULD BREAK THIS.
DATA_PHASES=0 -- DECLARED FLOOR, not a sentinel: src/data/api.py::data_plan resolves `max(2, int(dat.phases))` under the comment 'FLOORED AT 2 AT THIS READ SITE. One phase cannot have anything FADE, and `faded` is read off the last phase, so PHASES=1 makes the unlearn test skip itself as vacuous', and src/data/levers.py::DATALevers states the same floor as a port requirement the declaration cannot express. Measured: 0 yields schedule=((0,1),(2,3)) and counters {'data.phase_resolved': 2}, so the RESOLVED count is printed and the substitution is visible in the report. Recorded here rather than as a defect because it is documented in two places and reported; but the ruling phase should know the rewrite is SILENT at the moment it happens -- there is no Gate and no warning, only the resolved counter -- and that the same clamp swallows PHASES=1.
DATA_N_PROCESSES=0 -- REFUSED BY NAME on the arm where it means something and legitimately INERT on the other. On DATA_SOURCE=synthetic: 'CorpusError: DATA_N_PROCESSES=0: at least one synthetic process is required to produce a stream. Refused rather than silently returning zero areas.' On DATA_SOURCE=real it is inert BY DECLARATION -- the help text scopes it: 'How many synthetic Markov processes the stream is generated from, on DATA_SOURCE=synthetic only', and the comment demands the real path leave it alone rather than overwrite it. Verified inert on real (plan and stream identical to the real baseline).
DATA_VAL_CAP=0 -- REFUSED BY NAME on real: 'area 'eng' computed a 0-byte held-out block: min(int(2000000 * 0.05), 0) == 0 from DATA_HOLDOUT_FRAC=0.05 and DATA_VAL_CAP=0 ... raise DATA_HOLDOUT_FRAC or DATA_VAL_CAP'. Inert on synthetic, honestly: 'Gate data.val_cap_trip: UNREACHABLE (None vs 4000000) -- DATA_SOURCE=synthetic: with nothing held out there is no block for DATA_VAL_CAP to bind'. This is the model the rest of the surface should be measured against.
DATA_HOLDOUT_FRAC=0 -- REFUSED BY NAME on real, by the message quoted above, naming both levers and printing the arithmetic. Inert on synthetic because src/data/api.py::open_areas sets n_hold=0 unconditionally on that arm and the gate says so.
DATA_SEG_MIN=0 and DATA_SEG_MAX=0 -- REFUSED BY NAME at src/data/api.py::draw_stream: 'DATA_SEG_MIN=0 and DATA_SEG_MAX=1800: a segment must be at least one byte and the minimum may not exceed the maximum. Refused here rather than clamped, because a clamp would make the banner print a segment length the run did not use.'
DATA_EXPOSURE_MAX=0, DATA_EXPOSURE_SKEW=0, DATA_EXPOSURE_MAX=-inf, DATA_EXPOSURE_SKEW=-inf -- ACCEPTED and ARITHMETICALLY HONEST: the gate genuinely FIRES (0.75 > 0.0, 0.75 > -inf), which is the 'flag every plan' configuration, and the printed line is true. NOT A DECLARED SENTINEL: src/data/levers.py::DATALevers says only 'above which the data plan is flagged' and there is no 0 or -inf branch in src/data/api.py::data_plan. Listed here because a central refusal of 0 or -inf would remove a configuration that today behaves correctly and reports correctly -- but the ruling phase should not read this as 'the tree declares a meaning here', because it does not.
EVAL_CURVE_EVERY=0 -- ACCEPTED, MEANING EXPLICITLY UNDECLARED, AND THE UNDECLAREDNESS IS ITSELF DECLARED. src/eval/api.py::curve_period says in as many words: 'ZERO IS NOT TOUCHED, AND WHAT ZERO MEANS HERE IS NOT DECIDED BY THIS GUARD. Unlike CKPT.every (0 disables periodic saving, in the lever's own help text) and MEM.rekey_every (0 DISARMS, in memory/api.py::maintain), EVAL_CURVE_EVERY=0 has NO declared meaning ... The test below is strictly `< 0`, so whatever the tree eventually rules 0 to mean, it still reaches the same readers it reaches today.' Measured: curve_period returns Windows(0) and spine/derive.py::cadences_that_cannot_fire reports [('curve', 0, 0)] -- reported, not silent, by a function whose own comment says a period of zero or less 'IS A SENTINEL, AND IT MUST BE REPORTED, NOT SKIPPED'. The firing consumer (train/api.py::Cadences.due) is a P4 stub, so nothing fires either way today. A central rule refusing 0 would pre-empt a ruling EVAL has deliberately left open.
NOTHING ON THIS SURFACE DECLARES nan, inf OR -inf AS A SENTINEL. All 26 lever declarations in src/eval/levers.py::EVALLevers and src/data/levers.py::DATALevers were read for this line. A central non-finite refusal in src/spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce would wrongly refuse ZERO cells in EVAL or DATA.
